answer: Agents stake a bond of opal tokens to register, and each epoch they must post a costly signal: a unique proof-of-work tied to their identity and an ivory-keyed signature that cannot be reused or transferred. Duplicating an identity means locking a fresh bond and burning compute for every clone, so a sybil swarm's cost scales linearly while honest agents recover their stake. Peers verify the ivory signatures, slash bonds on replay, and reject any opal deposit lacking valid work, making mass fake identities economically irrational.
